exchanges.speaker: Pilot
exchanges.text: Guangzhou Control, Cathay two five one, encountering moderate chop Flight Level three fife zero, request descent to Flight Level three wun zero.
exchanges.meaning: Reports turbulence intensity and requests a level change to escape the chop.

exchanges.speaker: ATC
exchanges.text: Cathay two five one, Guangzhou Control, unable Flight Level three wun zero due traffic, descend to Flight Level three tree zero, report reaching.
exchanges.meaning: Alternative descent clearance denied at the requested level due to traffic.

exchanges.speaker: Pilot
exchanges.text: Descend to Flight Level three tree zero, report reaching, Cathay two five one.
exchanges.meaning: Readback of the descent clearance with the report-reaching requirement.

exchanges.speaker: ATC
exchanges.text: Cathay two five one, request PIREP, confirm turbulence intensity and conditions.
exchanges.meaning: ATC requests a standardized pilot weather report to warn downstream traffic.

exchanges.speaker: Pilot
exchanges.text: Guangzhou Control, Cathay two five one, PIREP: Boeing seven seven seven, position SIKOU at zero fow-er two zero, Flight Level three fife zero, moderate clear air turbulence, airspeed fluctuating plus minus ten knots.
exchanges.meaning: The mandatory PIREP sequence: aircraft type, position, time, flight level, turbulence intensity, airspeed fluctuation.

exchanges.speaker: ATC
exchanges.text: Cathay two five one, roger PIREP, thank you.
exchanges.meaning: ATC acknowledges the pilot weather report.

vocabulary.definition: Invisible high-altitude turbulence caused by wind shear at jet-stream boundaries, undetectable by weather radar.
Apparent strain against seatbelts; liquids splash; airspeed varies 10–15 knots.
Violent forces; momentarily out of control; walking impossible; immediate level change required.
Pilot Weather Report: standardized voice sequence of aircraft type, location, time, flight level, turbulence intensity and airspeed fluctuations.
The designated speed flown in turbulence, providing structural margin against stall and overstress.
The narrow speed band near an airliner's ceiling between low-speed stall and high-speed Mach buffet.

quiz.question: Which turbulence classification corresponds to conditions where occupants are forced violently against seatbelts, unsecured objects are tossed about, and momentary loss of aircraft control occurs?
quiz.explanation: Under ICAO criteria, severe turbulence is characterized by large, abrupt changes in altitude/attitude, large airspeed variations, and momentary loss of aircraft control.

quiz.question: What is the primary piloting technique recommended when penetrating severe turbulence in transport category aircraft?
options: Aggressively fight the autopilot to maintain exact target altitude.
Maintain wings level, control pitch attitude with smooth inputs, and allow altitude and airspeed to fluctuate within safe margins at Turbulence Penetration Speed.
Immediately deploy full speedbrakes to slow below stall speed.
Retract flaps and climb at maximum angle of climb (V_x).
quiz.explanation: Attempting to hold altitude strictly in severe turbulence causes severe structural load factors (G-forces). Pilots fly the certified turbulence penetration speed (V_RA), fly attitude, and allow the aircraft to ride the waves.

sections.heading: Section 2: Core Learning Content & Vocabulary Table
sections.body:
| Phrase / Command | ICAO Standard Definition | Operational Example |
|---|---|
| Request descent/climb due chop | Requesting level change due to rapid rhythmic jolts/bumps. | "Request descent FL310 due chop." |
| Moderate turbulence | Apparent strain against seatbelts; liquids splash; airspeed varies. | Airspeed fluctuates 10–15 knots. |
| Severe turbulence | Violent forces; momentarily out of control; walking impossible. | Immediate level change required. |
| PIREP (Pilot Weather Report) | Standardized voice report detailing in-flight weather hazards. | Mandatory reporting sequence to ATC. |
| Turbulence Penetration Speed | Designated speed (V_RA / M_RA) providing structural margin. | Flown to prevent stall or overstress. |

sections.heading: Section 8: Spaced Repetition Review Drill
sections.body:
- Day 21 Review (+1d): severe convective thunderstorm cells above FL200 require a minimum lateral clearance of 20 nautical miles.
- Day 17 Review (+7d): semicircular cruising rule — Eastbound tracks (000°–179°) fly ODD flight levels, Westbound (180°–359°) fly EVEN flight levels. RVSM separation is 1,000 feet.

sections.heading: Section 9: Fun Aviation Fact — Coffin Corner
sections.body: Near an airliner's maximum ceiling (e.g. FL410), the margin between low-speed aerodynamic stall and high-speed Mach buffet narrows to just a few knots — a zone pilots dub the "Coffin Corner"! If severe turbulence hits an aircraft in the coffin corner, an updraft slowing the plane by 10 knots triggers a stall, while a sudden 10-knot gust pushes it past maximum operating Mach (M_MO). That is why airliners immediately request descent upon encountering high-altitude chop!
